capabilities.title: Connections API, status and scoped termination
capabilities.persisted_state_or_side_effect: Scoped connection observations, an actor-bound PostgreSQL idempotency receipt whose ambiguous tombstone never expires automatically, bounded-TTL terminal receipts, and deterministic database audit events for privileged drop/reconciliation outcomes.
capabilities.retry_concurrency_contract: Drop is sent upstream at most once. Transport/5xx ambiguity is recorded as outcome_unknown with retry_allowed=false because upstream exposes no idempotency or exact reconciliation key. A trusted global Admin may later commit an immutable accepted/rejected decision from independent provider or postcondition evidence without requiring the receipt HMAC key.

backend.rbac_tenant_rationale: The exact 3.4.3 async read and single-attempt drop contract is implemented for Admin, Partner and Customer. Read jobs remain actor-bound in Redis, while drop receipts are committed to PostgreSQL before provider I/O with domain-separated HMAC key/scope/payload material. Customer identity is resolved through the exact reconciliation ledger; Partner requires exclusive exact node and service-identity grants. Unknown receipts have no automatic expiry; Admin-only exact-ID reconciliation uses SELECT FOR UPDATE, server-time TTL and a required sanitized audit in one transaction, remains available without the HMAC key, and never accepts raw key/scope/IP/provider payload. Downgrade retains receipt rows and re-upgrade validates the exact schema before grant DDL. The remaining gap is production-like provider/database runtime evidence.

It also provides a bounded unresolved-receipt queue with paging, strict accepted/rejected reason compatibility, a bounded CASE/INC/REQ/TKT/RW reference and explicit reconciliation confirmation. It exposes no TTL, HMAC, scope or raw-provider-payload input, and blocks mutation retry after error until refresh or a different receipt is selected.
